question.text: Which one of the following is the correct <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>PV</mi></math> vs <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">P</mi></math> plot at constant temperature for an ideal gas ? ( <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">P</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">V</mi></math> stand for pressure and volume of the gas respectively)

solution.text:
From ideal gas equation
PV=nRT [At constant temperature for fixed amount of ideal gas]
PV=constant
So, As P↑⇒PV remain constant.
